claim.quote: The "blind analysis" of all topologies yields no evidence for an oscillation signal.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published in Nucl. Phys. B 611 (2001) 3.

key_value_text.quote: sets a 90% C.L. allowed region in the sin^2(2theta)-Delta m^2 plane which includes sin^2(2theta)<3.3 x 10^{-4} at large Delta m^2 and Delta m^2 < 0.7 eV^2/c^4 at sin^2(2theta)=1
key_value_text.value: sin^2(2 theta) < 3.3e-4 at large delta m^2 and delta m^2 < 0.7 eV^2/c^4 at sin^2(2 theta) = 1 (90 % CL, nu_mu -> nu_tau)

name: Final NOMAD results on nu_mu->nu_tau and nu_e->nu_tau oscillations including a new search for nu_tau appearance using hadronic tau decays

significance.quote: this sets a 90% C.L. allowed region

summary.plain: Using all of its data and a new analysis of tau decays into hadrons, NOMAD again saw no sign of muon neutrinos turning into tau neutrinos. For large mass differences the mixing is below about 0.00033 (90 % confidence).
summary.technical: Full-statistics nu_tau appearance search with a new unified analysis of hadronic tau decays and a blind analysis of all topologies: no oscillation signal; 90 % CL region includes sin^2(2 theta) < 3.3e-4 at large delta m^2 and delta m^2 < 0.7 eV^2/c^4 at maximal mixing (nu_mu -> nu_tau); sin^2(2 theta) < 1.5e-2 and delta m^2 < 5.9 eV^2/c^4 for nu_e -> nu_tau.

title: Final NOMAD results on nu_mu->nu_tau and nu_e->nu_tau oscillations including a new search for nu_tau appearance using hadronic tau decays
why_it_matters: The tightest limit on nu_mu to nu_tau mixing at large delta m^2 from any experiment, ruling out the cosmologically motivated range of eV-scale tau-neutrino masses that the experiment was designed to test.
